questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of the Parallelogram Spanned by Two Non-Parallel Vectors
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13972686/assets/555cdb44522fab12ad67b54042ee4e47a085802df65c2b32a512eace16b92dd4.png)

Calculate the area of the parallelogram in the figure.
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we get the vectors

$$
\text{u}=⟨1,2⟩,\,\text{v}=⟨2,-1⟩.
$$

First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)-2\cdot 2 \\  & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A=|-5\,|=5
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\text{u}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ and $\text{v}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & \frac{\sqrt{5}}{3} \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & \frac{\sqrt{5}}{3} \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot 0-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A=|\,0\,|=0
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\text{u}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $\text{v}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -\frac{3}{2} \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -\frac{3}{2} \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot 1-(-\frac{3}{2})\cdot (-2) \\  & =3-3 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A=|\,0\,|=0
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of the Parallelogram Spanned by Two Non-Parallel Vectors
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we get the vectors

$$
\text{u}=⟨4,-1⟩,\,\text{v}=⟨-2,-3⟩.
$$

First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot (-3)-(-2)\cdot (-1) \\  & =-12-2 \\  & =-14\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A=|-14|=14
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of the Parallelogram Spanned by Two Parallel Vectors
questions.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} & a \\ -5 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} & a \\ -5 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot 6-a\cdot (-5) \\  & =9+5a\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, setting the expression for the determinant equal to $0$ and solving for $a,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9+5a & =0 \\ 5a & =-9 \\ a & =-\frac{9}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
